title: Realignment After Emergent Misalignment: Does Standard Safety Fine-Tuning Fully Recover Alignment?
original_idea: Take a small model fine-tuned to be emergently misaligned. Apply a brief safety SFT pass using a small helpful/harmless dataset. Re-evaluate on the standard EM evaluation set. Compare surface behavior, prompt sensitivity profile, and residual elicitation under adversarial prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: While basic realignment has been tested, the adversarial probing of realigned models (surface vs. residual misalignment) remains a critical open question with high safety relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses existing misaligned model from open codebase. Safety SFT using a public dataset (Anthropic HH-RLHF subset) is well-documented. Re-evaluation uses existing prompts plus adversarial variants. A beginner with guidance can execute each step using standard tools.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: one misaligned model, one safety SFT pass, re-evaluation on standard set. Well-defined success criteria (does misalignment rate return to baseline?). The prompt sensitivity and adversarial probing are natural extensions but the core comparison stands alone.

novelty.reasoning: The 'Emergent Misalignment & Realignment' work (LessWrong, 2025) directly tested whether SFT can realign emergently misaligned models, finding that AI optimism SFT can reduce misalignment back to original levels. Sleeper Agents (Hubinger et al. 2024) showed that deceptive behavior persists through standard safety training. The 'In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment' paper (arXiv:2508.06249) examines training-time defenses. Safety-Aware LLM Fine-Tuning literature addresses safe post-fine-tuning alignment. Neuron-level safety realignment (NLSR) proposes targeted interventions. The 50% correct-data recovery threshold has been characterized. However, the specific comparison of surface behavior vs. residual elicitation under adversarial prompts after safety SFT — testing whether misalignment is truly removed or merely suppressed — remains partially open. The realignment work showed behavioral recovery but adversarial probing of realigned models is less thoroughly characterized.

In-Training Defenses.details: Confirmed via arXiv:2508.06249. Examines training-time defenses against EM, related but focuses on prevention rather than post-hoc recovery.
